definition: doing what a person in authority tells you to do
example: Our first subject is obedience.

definition: a person who offers to take part in something without being forced
example: You are a volunteer for a study of memory.

definition: accepted as having the right to give orders or make decisions
example: Yale is a famous and legitimate institution.

definition: a person who secretly works with the researcher while pretending to be an ordinary participant
example: In fact he is a confederate: an actor who works for the experimenter.

definition: to pause before you do something because you are not sure
example: If you hesitate, the experimenter answers with a prod.

definition: a short push; here, a standard sentence that tells someone to go on
example: The experimenter answers with a prod.

definition: strong feelings of worry, pain or unhappiness
example: Many volunteers showed clear distress.

definition: making someone believe something that is not true
example: The whole study relied on deception.

definition: a fixed series of actions that are done in a particular order
example: Forty men took part in a procedure at Yale.

definition: the result of something
example: The outcome was far higher than the experts had predicted.

definition: to do what you are told or asked to do
example: Ordinary people may comply with an authority.

definition: worried and upset
example: Many volunteers were visibly troubled.

definition: good enough to be allowed
example: Was the research itself acceptable?

definition: to vary between a lowest and a highest value
example: The share ranged from 28 to 91 per cent.

definition: normal or usual for a kind of thing
example: Harm that is more typical of modern life.

definition: doubting whether something is true or good
example: Be sceptical of the headline and of its critics.

definition: the health, safety and happiness of a person or group
example: Her main objection was about the volunteers' welfare.

definition: a person's agreement to take part after being told honestly what will happen
example: They had not given real informed consent.

definition: to explain the true purpose of a study to participants after it has finished
example: Every volunteer was told the truth in a debrief.

definition: a request that speaks to a person's values or feelings
example: Appeals to the value of science worked better than orders.

definition: a collection of old documents and records
example: A third kind of criticism came from the archive.

definition: a public argument about something that people strongly disagree about
example: Here is a summary of the ethical controversy.

definition: an explanation of what something means
example: The second objection is about interpretation.

definition: a group of people chosen to make decisions or give advice
example: Research ethics committees became routine.

definition: to make something no longer valid or true
example: Neither objection cancels the study.

definition: to feel that you share the aims or feelings of a person or group
example: The volunteers identified with the scientific cause.

definition: to perform or organise something again
example: They restaged the procedure for a film.

definition: complicated and not clear or tidy
example: The archive tells a messier story.

definition: a version of a procedure in which one thing is changed
example: Milgram ran about twenty variations of the study.

definition: a rule or measure that protects people from harm
example: Stopping at 150 volts was a reasonable safeguard.

definition: statistically significant: unlikely to be caused by chance alone
example: The difference was not statistically significant.

definition: a new study that repeats an earlier study to check its result
example: This is a partial replication.

definition: a warning that a statement is only true under certain conditions
example: Every claim needs a caveat.

definition: a statement that something is true, especially one that is not yet proved
example: Let us test some claims.

definition: strong and not easily broken or disproved
example: The finding appears robust in a limited sense.

definition: to say that something is true for a whole group or for all situations
example: The finding cannot be generalised without caution.

definition: belonging to the present time
example: The result is contemporary as well as historical.

definition: to stay in the same state or place
example: Three things seem to remain.

definition: to get the same result again by repeating a study
example: Can the result be reproduced?

definition: connected with what is morally right
example: Researchers now use ethical designs.

definition: an opinion or decision about something, especially after thinking carefully
example: You answered a study of visual judgement.

definition: one attempt or round of a test
example: Each card is a new trial.

definition: most of the people in a group
example: The actors formed a majority.

definition: agreed by everybody, with no exception
example: On twelve cards the actors were unanimous.

definition: to give way to pressure and do what others want
example: Three quarters of the volunteers yielded to the group at least once.

definition: changing what you say or do to match a group
example: The subject of this case is conformity.

definition: a nervous, uncomfortable feeling when something is uncertain or stressful
example: Many volunteers showed tension.

definition: to change something so that it is no longer true or accurate
example: Group pressure can distort judgement.

definition: not clear, because it can be understood in more than one way
example: Sherif used an ambiguous task.

definition: a guess about a size, amount or value
example: Their estimates moved towards the group's.

definition: easy to see or understand
example: The answer is obvious.

definition: the ability to think and act without being controlled by others
example: The word independence comes first in the title.

definition: to understand something in the wrong way
example: Asch's work was misinterpreted over the years.

definition: a book that teaches a subject at school or university
example: Griggs checked twenty recent textbooks.

definition: without your name or identity being known
example: They answered anonymously in separate booths.

definition: fair, giving the right weight to all sides
example: Which version reports the result in the most balanced way?

definition: a small closed space for one person, for example for voting or for a test
example: They answered in separate booths.

definition: choosing only some things and leaving others out
example: Selective reporting gives more space to one half of the result.

definition: importance or influence given to something
example: The two numbers were not given the same weight.

definition: a university student who is studying for a first degree
example: They tested Japanese undergraduates.

definition: a person who supports you, especially against opposition
example: The volunteer had an ally.

definition: to stop rising or falling and stay at about the same level
example: The pull rose to 31.8 per cent and then levelled off.

definition: a small group chosen to represent a larger group
example: The sample of studies was uneven.

definition: a study that combines the results of many earlier studies
example: Bond and Smith published a meta-analysis of 133 studies.

definition: valuing the group and its harmony more than the individual
example: In more collectivist countries conformity was higher.

definition: to become smaller, weaker or less
example: In the United States, conformity had declined since the 1950s.

definition: the main point of a story, put in a short form
example: The textbook headline is simpler than the evidence.

definition: a fixed, simple idea about a group of people
example: Later work has not confirmed the stereotype.

definition: to use power or influence to affect something
example: Do online groups exert the same pressure?

definition: the act of accepting the power or control of another person
example: Obedience may be less about blind submission than about identification with a cause.

definition: a weakness or a point beyond which something cannot be trusted or used
example: Both studies have clear limitations.

definition: an idea about the reason for something that has not yet been proved
example: A hypothesis about the reasons is still being tested.

definition: used to compare two facts and show that they are different
example: Case 1 studied an authority, whereas Case 2 studied a group.

definition: in the same way
example: Similarly, both studies used deception.

definition: used to show a clear difference between two things
example: In contrast to Case 1, Case 2 produced more independent answers.

definition: a habit or a likely way of behaving
example: Why might a tendency to follow the group exist at all?

definition: a feature that helps a living thing to survive in its environment
example: Researchers treat it as a possible adaptation.
